response.title: how long will a power station run an electric blanket
response.answer:
A portable power station can run an electric blanket for about 4–20 hours, depending on the battery capacity, blanket wattage, and heat setting.

Most electric blankets consume 50–150 watts at full power, but may average considerably less on lower settings as the thermostat cycles.

markup:
A portable power station can run an electric blanket for **about 4–20 hours**, depending on the battery capacity, blanket wattage, and heat setting.

Most electric blankets consume **50–150 watts** at full power, but may average considerably less on lower settings as the thermostat cycles.

## Estimated runtime

Assuming 85% usable battery energy (including inverter losses):

| Power station capacity | 50W blanket | 100W blanket | 150W blanket |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 256Wh | 4.4 hrs | 2.2 hrs | 1.5 hrs |
| 500Wh | 8.5 hrs | 4.3 hrs | 2.8 hrs |
| 768Wh | 13.1 hrs | 6.5 hrs | 4.4 hrs |
| 1,024Wh | 17.4 hrs | 8.7 hrs | 5.8 hrs |
| 2,048Wh | 34.8 hrs | 17.4 hrs | 11.6 hrs |

These estimates assume continuous power consumption. Actual runtime may be longer if the blanket cycles on and off.

## Runtime calculator

{@body const [capacity,setCapacity] = DIL.useState("1024")}
{@body const [watts,setWatts] = DIL.useState(100)}
{@body const [eff,setEff] = DIL.useState(85)}
{@body const hours = Number(capacity)*eff/100/watts}
<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <form gap={3}>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>Power station battery capacity</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={capacity} onChange={setCapacity}>
        <radio value="256">256Wh</radio>
        <radio value="512">512Wh</radio>
        <radio value="1024">1,024Wh</radio>
        <radio value="2048">2,048Wh</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <divider color="subtle"/>
    <row align="center" justify="between">
      **Electric blanket power**
      <text weight="medium" tabularNums>{watts}W</text>
    </row>
    <slider min={20} max={200} step={10} value={watts} onChange={setWatts}/>
    <row align="center" justify="between">
      **Usable battery efficiency**
      <text weight="medium" tabularNums>{eff}%</text>
    </row>
    <slider min={70} max={95} step={5} value={eff} onChange={setEff}/>
  </form>
  <box background="surface-secondary" radius="lg" padding={3} align="center" gap={1}>
    <text color="secondary" weight="medium" size="xs">Estimated runtime</text>
    <title size="2xl" color="default" tabularNums>{hours.toFixed(1)} hours</title>
    <text color="secondary" size="xs">At {watts}W average consumption</text>
  </box>
</box>

## How to calculate it

\[
\text{Runtime (hours)}=\frac{\text{Battery Wh}\times0.85}{\text{Blanket Watts}}
\]

For example, a 1,024Wh power station running a 100W electric blanket would last approximately 8.7 hours.

**One important detail:** Electric blankets often cycle their heating elements. A blanket rated at 100W might average only 30–60W on a low setting, significantly extending runtime. Follow the blanket manufacturer's overnight-use instructions.

**What power station and electric blanket do you have?** Give me the models or their Wh and wattage ratings, and I can estimate how many hours they'll run together on low, medium, and high settings.
